name: Monthly bookkeeping
headline:
Good decisions start
with reliable books.
desc: Organized transactions, reconciled accounts, and a consistent view of your business. Monthly bookkeeping that helps you stay on top of the numbers.
audience: US business owners who want their books handled consistently, with less time spent chasing or organizing records.
scope: Monthly profit and loss and balance sheet
Open questions and exceptions highlighted for review
needs: Your legal entity and business model
Current accounting software and period to be covered
Bank and credit card accounts to reconcile
Prior financial statements and opening balances
deliver: A reconciled reporting period, financial statements, and a clear list of outstanding questions or next steps.

name: Accounting & reporting
headline:
More than a report.
A view you can use.
desc: Management reporting that connects your financial records to what is happening in the business: revenue, costs, margins, and cash.
audience: Owners who need more visibility than transaction processing alone can provide.
scope: Monthly financial statements and reporting schedules
Cash flow reporting and working capital visibility
Reporting structure suited to your business model
needs: Recent financial statements and trial balance
Chart of accounts and current reports
Revenue streams and major cost categories
Your reporting priorities and internal stakeholders
deliver: A reporting pack with the agreed financial statements, supporting schedules, and key items for discussion.

name: Fractional CFO advisory
headline:
A financial perspective
on your next move.
desc: Cash planning, budgeting, and financial analysis for business owners making decisions about growth, hiring, and investment.
audience: Founders and growing businesses that want regular financial oversight without adding a full-time finance leadership role.
scope: Cash flow forecasting and scenario planning
Financial decision support and planning discussions
needs: Current financial statements and cash position
Business model and growth priorities
Debt, fixed commitments, and planned investments
Existing budget, forecasts, and performance measures
deliver: An agreed planning model, reporting cadence, and decision-focused financial discussion.

name: QuickBooks setup & cleanup
tag: Get back to a clear starting point
headline:
Messy books?
Start with a plan.
desc: A structured review of your QuickBooks file, followed by a scoped cleanup, catch-up, or setup engagement.
audience: Businesses moving to QuickBooks Online, catching up on prior periods, or dealing with unreconciled balances and unclear records.
scope: QuickBooks Online setup and chart of accounts review
needs: Software, access role, and file history
Periods requiring setup or cleanup
Bank statements and available source documents
Prior returns or financial statements for reference
deliver: The agreed periods reviewed and organized, with reconciliations and a handover of remaining items.

name: Payroll coordination
headline:
Payroll, connected
to your books.
desc: Support organizing payroll inputs, coordinating with your payroll provider, and reconciling payroll activity in your accounting records.
audience: US businesses that want payroll and accounting to work together with clear responsibilities.
scope: Year-end information coordination with your provider
needs: Payroll provider and pay schedule
Employer and entity details
Payroll reports and relevant ledger balances
Agreed responsibilities for approvals and filings
deliver: Agreed payroll coordination and accounting support. Processing, filings, and provider responsibilities are confirmed in scope.

name: Tax-ready books & CPA support
headline:
Give your tax professional
a clearer starting point.
desc: Organized financial records and year-end schedules that help your CPA or tax preparer review the business and complete their work.
audience: Owners who want fewer last-minute document requests and better coordination between bookkeeping and their tax professional.
scope: Coordination on bookkeeping questions from your CPA
needs: Relevant financial year and legal entities
Your CPA or tax preparer contact, with permission
Current books and prior-year financials
Outstanding tax-preparer requests
deliver: An agreed year-end bookkeeping package and coordination on related questions. Tax filing or representation is separately scoped with the appropriate professional.
